name: Choosing a lift
description: Sizing, type and where to start.

questions.question: Which type of lift do I need for a private house?
questions.answer: For most villas of two to five levels, a machine-room-less home elevator is the right answer: it needs no plant room, fits a shaft from about 1,100 × 1,000 mm, and runs quietly enough to sit next to bedrooms. If the lift is going into an atrium or a double-height hall where it will be seen, a glazed capsule lift is worth the extra shaft.

questions.question: How much space does a lift actually need?
questions.answer: Less than most people assume. A compact four-passenger home lift needs an internal shaft from roughly 1,100 × 1,000 mm, a pit from 350 mm and about 2,600 mm of headroom above the top floor. A commercial eight-passenger car needs about 1,900 × 2,000 mm. Send us a floor plan and we will mark up what fits.

questions.question: What if my building has no lift shaft at all?
questions.answer: A self-supporting steel structure can be erected inside a stairwell void or against an external wall, carrying its own loads to a new pad at the base. We did exactly this at Kashi Yadhav's Residence — a four-storey occupied house that never had a shaft.

questions.question: How many people should the lift carry?
questions.answer: Size by the worst case, not the average. For a home, count the largest group that will realistically travel together — and if anyone may need a wheelchair, specify a car deep enough to turn in. For a commercial building, size against expected peak five-minute traffic rather than headcount.

questions.question: Traction or hydraulic — which is better?
questions.answer: Traction for almost everything: quieter, more efficient, better ride, more travel. Hydraulic earns its place on short travels where the structure cannot carry suspended load at the top of the shaft, or where a very heavy load moves a short distance.

questions.question: Can the lift match my interior?
questions.answer: Yes — that is usually the point. Wall material, flooring, ceiling, lighting, handrail and control panel are all specified separately. At Lacheta Nivas the car was detailed with the joinery, in antique brass with a marble floor.

questions.question: Do you work outside Hyderabad?
questions.answer: Yes. Hyderabad and the wider Telangana region are our core service area, and we take projects across South India where we can commit to the same installation and maintenance response. Tell us the location and we will say honestly whether we can support it.

questions.question: How long does a lift last?
questions.answer: A well-maintained passenger lift runs for 20 to 25 years before it needs modernisation, and modernisation usually means new drive, controller and interior on the existing shaft and rails rather than a full replacement.

name: Products & technology
description: Drives, controls and how the machine works.

questions.question: What does machine-room-less actually mean?
questions.answer: The traction machine mounts on the guide rails at the head of the shaft instead of in a room above it. The building gets that room back, and because the motor is gearless there is no gearbox, no gear oil and much less noise.

questions.question: Why is a gearless motor better than a geared one?
questions.answer: A gearless permanent-magnet motor drives the sheave directly. Removing the gearbox removes the main source of mechanical noise, the main heat load, and the oil changes. It is also more efficient, and with a regenerative drive it returns braking energy to the building.

questions.question: What is a VVVF drive?
questions.answer: Variable-voltage variable-frequency control. It shapes the motor's speed continuously, so starting and stopping follow a curve rather than a step. That is what makes a modern lift feel smooth, and it is what holds floor levelling within a few millimetres whether the car is full or empty.

questions.question: How accurate is floor levelling?
questions.answer: Within ±3 mm on our traction systems and ±5 mm on hydraulic, loaded or empty. That matters most in hospitals, where a trolley wheel will find any lip at the sill.

questions.question: How noisy is a lift inside the house?
questions.answer: A gearless MRL home lift runs under about 55 dB(A) inside the car at rated speed — conversation level. Most of what people remember as lift noise came from geared machines and relay controllers, neither of which we fit.

questions.question: Can I get a lift with a glass shaft?
questions.answer: Yes. Both the structural shaft and the car can be glazed, in toughened laminated glass so any failure stays in place. This is how the capsule lifts at Chilkuru Residence and Lekha Nilayam are built.

name: Installation
description: Survey, programme and what happens on site.

questions.question: How long does an installation take?
questions.answer: For a home lift with a ready shaft, typically three to five weeks on site after delivery. A retrofit that needs its own structure runs longer, and a commercial group of several cars is programmed floor by floor. We give you a dated programme before we start.

questions.question: What do you need from me before you can quote?
questions.answer: A floor plan and a section if you have them, the number of levels, the floor-to-floor heights, and what the lift is for. If there is an existing shaft, its internal dimensions and pit depth. Drawings can be uploaded with your enquiry.

questions.question: Do you do a site survey?
questions.answer: Always, before anything is manufactured. Shafts are rarely plumb and rarely the dimension on the drawing. The survey is where we find that out, not the installation.

questions.question: Who prepares the shaft?
questions.answer: Civil work — the shaft walls, the pit, waterproofing and the power supply to the controller position — is usually by the builder, to a drawing we issue. We can take on the structural shaft itself where there is none.

questions.question: Can a lift be installed in an occupied building?
questions.answer: Yes, and most of our retrofits are. Work is sequenced to keep the stair usable, and the noisy operations are programmed rather than sprung on the household.

questions.question: What power supply does a lift need?
questions.answer: Usually a three-phase 415 V supply to the controller position, sized to the drive. Some compact home lifts run on single-phase 230 V. We confirm the requirement at survey so the electrician can allow for it.

questions.question: What happens at handover?
questions.answer: Load testing to 125% of rated capacity, an overspeed and safety-gear trip test, levelling and door timing adjustment, statutory inspection paperwork, and a walkthrough with whoever will operate the building.

name: Safety
description: What protects you, and how it is proven.

questions.question: What happens in a power cut?
questions.answer: The automatic rescue device takes over on battery, drives the car at reduced speed to the nearest landing, opens the doors and keeps the cabin light and fan running. You are not waiting in the dark for the mains to return.

questions.question: What stops the lift falling?
questions.answer: Nothing about a lift depends on one component. The car hangs on multiple independent steel ropes, each rated well beyond the whole load. Above that, an overspeed governor watches the descent, and if the car ever exceeds the trip speed, progressive safety gear grips the guide rails mechanically and stops it.

questions.question: Can the doors close on someone?
questions.answer: A full-height infrared curtain across the entrance reopens the doors on any obstruction, with no contact needed. It sees a hand, a bag strap or a walking stick.

questions.question: What happens if there is a fire?
questions.answer: On a fire signal the car cancels all calls, returns to the designated evacuation landing, parks with its doors open and locks out normal operation until it is reset by the fire service.

questions.question: Is the lift tested before I get it?
questions.answer: Every car is load-tested to 125% of rated capacity and the overspeed governor and safety gear are tripped and verified before dispatch. The tests are then repeated on site after installation.

questions.question: What if someone is trapped?
questions.answer: Press the alarm. It connects to a battery-backed two-way intercom that reaches our service desk directly, independent of the building's power, 24 hours a day.

questions.question: What does an AMC cover?
questions.answer: Scheduled preventive visits, adjustment, lubrication, rope and brake inspection, safety testing, and priority breakdown response. Comprehensive contracts include parts; non-comprehensive ones bill parts separately.

questions.question: How often should a lift be serviced?
questions.answer: Monthly for commercial and healthcare installations, quarterly at minimum for a home lift. Frequency is set by usage, not by the calendar alone.

questions.question: How fast do you respond to a breakdown?
questions.answer: Our service desk is staffed 24/7 and we prioritise entrapments above everything else. Response times to site are set out in your maintenance contract.

questions.question: Do you service lifts you did not install?
questions.answer: Yes, subject to a survey. We need to see the equipment and its history before we can take responsibility for it, and we will tell you honestly if something needs putting right before a contract starts.

questions.question: Can an old lift be modernised instead of replaced?
questions.answer: Usually. Drive, controller, doors and interior can be replaced on the existing shaft, rails and structure — better ride and efficiency for a fraction of the disruption of a full replacement.

questions.question: Are spare parts available years later?
questions.answer: We hold parts for the systems we install and support them through their service life. This is one of the reasons we keep the range deliberately narrow.

name: Pricing & enquiry
description: Cost, quotes and what happens next.

questions.question: How much does a lift cost?
questions.answer: Honestly, it depends on travel, capacity, drive type and finish, and the range is wide enough that any single number quoted here would mislead you. Send the floors and the building type and we will come back with a real figure rather than a bracket.

questions.question: What drives the cost most?
questions.answer: Number of stops first, then capacity, then finish. Going from a standard stainless car to a brass or stone interior changes the price meaningfully; adding a floor changes it more.

questions.question: Is installation included in the quote?
questions.answer: Yes. Our quotes cover supply, installation and commissioning, and state clearly what is excluded — usually civil work, the power supply to the controller and any statutory fees.

questions.question: How long is a quote valid?
questions.answer: Typically 30 days, because steel and component pricing moves. The validity is stated on the quotation itself.

questions.question: What happens after I submit an enquiry?
questions.answer: We review the drawings and the brief, call you to fill in what the form could not, recommend a system with reasons, and then quote against that recommendation.

questions.question: How quickly will someone get back to me?
questions.answer: Within one working day for project enquiries. Service and breakdown calls are answered 24/7 on the service line.

questions.question: Can I upload drawings with my enquiry?
questions.answer: Yes — PDF, JPG, PNG, WEBP, DWG and DXF, up to six files of 10 MB each. Plans and sections are the two most useful things you can send.

questions.question: I have an existing lift, not a new project.
questions.answer: Use the service route rather than the project enquiry form. It reaches our service desk directly instead of the sales pipeline.

questions.question: Can I visit the factory?
questions.answer: Yes, by appointment. Seeing cars being fabricated and load-tested tells you more about a lift company than any brochure.

questions.question: Do you do site visits before quoting?
questions.answer: For anything beyond a straightforward new-build shaft, yes. It is the only reliable way to quote a retrofit.
